{{short description|Relates the topology of a complete non-archimedean field to its algebraic extensions}}
In [[number theory]], more specifically in [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]], '''Krasner's lemma''' is a basic result relating the [[topological space|topology]] of a [[complete field|complete]] [[non-archimedean field]] to its [[algebraic extension]]s.

==Statement==
Let ''K'' be a complete non-archimedean field and let {{overline|''K''}} be a [[separable closure]] of ''K''. Given an element α in {{overline|''K''}}, denote its [[Galois conjugate]]s by ''α''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''α''<sub>''n''</sub>. Krasner's lemma states:<ref>Lemma 8.1.6 of {{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2008}}</ref><ref>Lorenz (2008) p.78</ref>

{{block indent|1=if an element ''β'' of {{overline|''K''}} is such that
<math display="block">\left|\alpha-\beta\right|<\left|\alpha-\alpha_i\right|\text{ for }i=2,\dots,n </math>
then ''K''(''α'')&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''K''(''β'').}}

==Applications==
Krasner's lemma can be used to show that [[Completion (ring theory)|<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>-adic completion]] and separable closure of [[global field]]s commute.<ref>Proposition 8.1.5 of {{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2008}}</ref> In other words,  given <math>\mathfrak{p}</math> a [[algebraic number field#Places|prime]] of a global field ''L'', the separable closure of the <math>\mathfrak{p}</math>-adic completion of ''L'' equals the <math>\overline{\mathfrak{p}}</math>-adic completion of the separable closure of ''L'' (where <math>\overline{\mathfrak{p}}</math> is a prime of {{overline|''L''}} above <math>\mathfrak{p}</math>).

Another application is to proving that '''C'''<sub>p</sub>&mdash;the completion of the algebraic closure of '''Q'''<sub>p</sub>&mdash;is [[algebraically closed]].<ref>Proposition 10.3.2 of {{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2008}}</ref><ref>Lorenz (2008) p.80</ref>

==Generalization==
Krasner's lemma has the following generalization.<ref>Brink (2006), Theorem 6</ref>
Consider a monic polynomial 
<math display="block">f^*=\prod_{k=1}^n(X-\alpha_k^*)</math> 
of degree ''n'' > 1
with coefficients in a [[Henselian field]] (''K'', ''v'') and roots in the
algebraic closure {{overline|''K''}}. Let ''I'' and ''J'' be two disjoint,
non-empty sets with union {1,...,''n''}. Moreover, consider a
polynomial 
<math display="block">g=\prod_{i\in I}(X-\alpha_i)</math>
with coefficients and roots in {{overline|''K''}}. Assume
<math display="block">\forall i\in I\forall j\in J: v(\alpha_i-\alpha_i^*)>v(\alpha_i^*-\alpha_j^*).</math>
Then the coefficients of the polynomials
<math display="block">g^*:=\prod_{i\in I}(X-\alpha_i^*),\ h^*:=\prod_{j\in J}(X-\alpha_j^*)</math>
are contained in the field extension of ''K'' generated by the
coefficients of ''g''. (The original Krasner's lemma corresponds to the situation where ''g'' has degree 1.)
